ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p139/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p139/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p139/r7.claim: God made earthly adornment to test which people act best; not everyone follows the messengers equally, so the Prophet need not grieve, and blessings are not withdrawn even from disbelievers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p139/r7.anchor: لأنه تعالى أخبر أنه خلق ما على الأرض من الزينة للابتلاء والاختبار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p139/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p139/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p139/r8.claim: Jaʿalnā here means created; mā apparently refers broadly to non-rational things, and every thing has adornment suited to it.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p139/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p139/r9.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p139/r9.claim: Some exclude harmful animals, stones, and plants from adornment; defenders of the general reading say their creation, workmanship, and perfection make them beautiful.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p139/r9.anchor: وقيل: لا يدخل في ذلك ما كان فيه إيذاء من حيوان وحجر ونبات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p139/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p139/r10.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p139/r10.claim: Other restricted readings identify the adornment with trees and rivers, flowering plants, animals, or precious metals and gems.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p139/r10.anchor: وقيل: المراد بما هنا خصوص ما لا بعقل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p139/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p139/r11.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p139/r11.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī limits the phrase to worldly luxuries and attractive things fit to adorn the earth and its people.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p139/r11.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: ما على الأرض يعني ما يصلح أن يكون زينة لها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p139/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p139/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p139/r12.claim: An anonymous report says the adornment included blessings, clothing, fruit, greenery, and water.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p139/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p139/r13.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p139/r13.claim: A rational reading of mā is attributed to Mujāhid, who says it means men, and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr transmits this from Ibn ʿAbbās.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p139/r13.anchor: فعن مجاهد هو الرجال وقاله ابن جبير عن ابن عباس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p139/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p139/r14.speaker: عكرمة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p139/r14.claim: ʿIkrima says the earthly adornment means rulers, scholars, and commanders.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p139/r14.anchor: وروى عكرمة أن الزينة الخلفاء والعلماء والأمراء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p139/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p139/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p139/r15.claim: Zīnata is a circumstantial accusative or purpose object if jaʿalnā means created; if it means made into, it is the second object.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p139/r15.anchor: وانتصب زينة على الحال أو على المفعول من أجله إن كان جعلنا بمعنى خلقنا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r1.claim: The lām in li-nabluwahum attaches to jaʿalnā; testing is interpreted relative to God, and hum refers to mā if rational or else the people understood from context.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r1.anchor: والابتلاء الاختبار وهو متأول بالنسبة إلى الله تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r2.claim: Ayyuhum may be a nominative pronoun phrase, with ahsanu as predicate and the whole question as the object of li-nabluwahum; testing is construed like knowing because it causes knowledge.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r3.speaker: الحوفي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r3.claim: Al-Ḥawfī takes the clause as an interrogative sentence with a subject and predicate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r3.anchor: وإلى أن الجملة استفهامية مبتدأ وخبر ذهب الحوفي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r4.speaker: سيبويه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r4.claim: Under Sībawayh’s analysis, ayyuhum may be built in the nominative because it meets the conditions for deleting the head of its relative clause; ahsanu predicates an omitted huwa, and the phrase substitutes for the pronoun in nabluwahum.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r4.anchor: ويحتمل أن تكون الضمة فيها بناء على مذهب سيبويه لوجود شرط جواز البناء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r5.speaker: الثوري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r5.claim: Al-Thawrī says best in deeds means most ascetic toward the world.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r5.anchor: وقال الثوري أحسنهم عملا أزهدهم فيها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r6.speaker: أبو عاصم العسقلاني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r6.claim: Abū ʿĀṣim al-ʿAsqalānī says it means the one who leaves the world most readily.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r6.anchor: وقال أبو عاصم العسقلاني: أترك لها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī defines good action as asceticism and avoiding delusion by worldly adornment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r7.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: حسن العمل الزهد فيها وترك الاغترار بها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r8.speaker: أبو بكر غالب بن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r8.claim: Abū Bakr Ghālib ibn ʿAṭiyya says it is taking one’s due with faith, performing obligations, avoiding prohibitions, and increasing voluntary good works.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r8.anchor: وقال أبو بكر غالب بن عطية: أحسن العمل أخذ بحق مع الإيمان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r9.speaker: الكلبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r9.claim: Al-Kalbī says best in deeds means best in obedience.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r10.speaker: القاسم بن محمد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r10.claim: Al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad says the adornment includes prophets and scholars, testing which of their recipients and imitators responds and accepts best.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r10.anchor: وقال القاسم بن محمد ما عليها من الأنبياء والعلماء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r11.speaker: سهل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r11.claim: Sahl says best action means the finest reliance on God amid worldly adornment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r11.anchor: وقال سهل: أحسن توكلا علينا فيها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r12.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r12.claim: Another view defines the best as the purest in heart and finest in demeanor.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r13.speaker: ابن إسحاق
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r13.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says best means most faithful to God’s command and most active in obedience.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r13.anchor: وقال ابن إسحاق: أيهم أتبع لأمري وأعمل بطاعتي

ALUSI-FULL:v15p257/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p257/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p257/r14.claim: The rivers, trees, minerals, and animals on earth are its adornment for its inhabitants; the test of best action turns that adornment into a mirror for contemplating divine majesty and beauty.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p257/r14.anchor: من الأنهار الأشجار والمعادن والحيوانات ( زينة لها ( أي لأهلها ( لنبلوهم أيهم أحسن عملا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p258/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p258/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
ALUSI-FULL:v15p258/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ defines good action as turning away from everything else.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p258/r1.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء : حسن العمل الاعتراض عن الكل

ALUSI-FULL:v15p258/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p258/r2.speaker: الجنيد
ALUSI-FULL:v15p258/r2.claim: Al-Junayd says good action is to take up worldly adornment without becoming occupied by it.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p258/r2.anchor: وقال الجنيد : حسن العمل اتخاذ ذلك وعدم الاشتغال به

ALUSI-FULL:v15p258/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p258/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p258/r3.claim: Some say God's knowers and lovers adorn the earth, and good action is to regard them with reverence.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p258/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم : أهل المعرفة بالله تعالى والمحبة له هم زينة الأرض وحسن العمل النظر إليهم بالحرمة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p659/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p659/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p659/r1.claim: Earth's adornment comprises worldly luxuries and pleasing things made for earth and its inhabitants; the test asks who acts best, with the best action being detachment rather than delusion by them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p659/r1.anchor: ما يصلح أن يكون زينة لها ولأهلها من زخارف الدنيا

ASAD-NOTES:18:intro/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:intro/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:18:intro/r1.claim: The surah's parables contrast faith in God with undue attachment to worldly life; its key idea is that earthly beauty tests people, most clearly in the rich and poor men story.
ASAD-NOTES:18:intro/r1.anchor: and the key-phrase of the whole surah is the statement in verse 7,

TABATABAI:18:23/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:23/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:23/r4.claim: The cave sleepers mirror humanity absorbed in earthly adornment: people will awaken from worldly life and reckon its long span as a day or part of one.
TABATABAI:18:23/r4.anchor: ليس ذلك كله إلا آية إلهية هي نظيرة ما جرى على أصحاب الكهف

TABATABAI:18:27/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:27/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:27/r3.claim: Because the verse resumes the pre-story argument, “recite” can coordinate with the earlier statement about earthly adornment; the unchanged words and absence of refuge then explain the command.
TABATABAI:18:27/r3.anchor: رجوع إلى ما قبل القصة وعليه فالأنسب أن يكون قوله

TABATABAI:18:42-44#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:42-44#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:42-44#2/r4.claim: God is better in reward and outcome because His reality endures, while worldly adornments fade; since people need something to rely on for their affairs, their Lord is better.
TABATABAI:18:42-44#2/r4.anchor: لأنه سبحانه هو الحق الثابت الذي لا يفنى ولا يزول

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p172/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p172/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p172/r1.claim: Earth's adornments are a test of which people obey God best, although God already knows what they will do.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p172/r1.anchor: قوله: {إنا جعلنا ما على الأرض زينة لها لنبلوهم} [الكهف: 7] لنختبرهم.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The earth’s adornment is a test of who uses reason to seek the Hereafter and who follows desire in seeking worldly life.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: This world is a place of trial and test

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Worldly pleasures and status are immediately available while their pains are hidden; Hereafter’s successes remain unseen and pursuing them brings worldly hardships, making this a severe test.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: All its pleasures are at hand and easy to attain while its pains are hidden

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Only perceptive people resist worldly lures rather than sacrifice the Hereafter’s blessings for them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Only those will sail through it who are perspicacious enough not to be misled by these worldly lures

BURSEVI:v5p167#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p167#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p167#2/r5.claim: Animals, plants, and minerals on earth are its adornment and the adornment of its inhabitants.

BURSEVI:v5p167#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p167#2/r6.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p167#2/r6.claim: God beautified worldly attractions to suit people's natures and made them a trial, exposing who does best by leaving them and opposing desire for God's pleasure.
BURSEVI:v5p167#2/r6.anchor: زينا الدنيا وشهواتها للخلق ملاءمة لطباعهم وجعلناها محل ابتلاء

BURSEVI:v5p167#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p167#2/r7.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p167#2/r7.claim: The worst response turns away from God and enduring good deeds, embracing transient, corrupt worldly things.
BURSEVI:v5p167#2/r7.anchor: في الإعراض عن الله وما عنده من الباقيات الصالحات والإقبال على الدنيا وما فيها

BURSEVI:v5p167#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p167#2/r8.speaker: الإرشاد
BURSEVI:v5p167#2/r8.claim: The interrogative ayy is a nominative subject, aḥsan is its predicate, and ʿamalan is a specification; the whole clause is governed by the testing verb.
BURSEVI:v5p167#2/r8.anchor: مرفوعة بالابتداء وأحسن خبرها وعملا تمييز

BURSEVI:v5p167#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p167#2/r9.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v5p167#2/r9.claim: Some say the phrase means God's prophets, scholars, or Qur'an preservers adorn the earth; others say God's men adorn it because the world's continuance depends on them.
BURSEVI:v5p167#2/r9.anchor: آرايش زمين برجال الله است ازان روى كه قيام عالم بوجود شريف ايشان بازبسته است

ALUSI-FULL:v15p206/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p206/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p206/r1.claim: The apparent scope of “whatever is on earth” includes all nonrational things—animals, plants, and minerals—as adornment for the earth and its people, each according to its nature.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p206/r1.anchor: الظاهر عموم ما جميع ما لا يعقل أي سواء كان حيوانا أو نباتا أو معدنا أي جعلنا جميع ما عليها

ALUSI-FULL:v15p206/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p206/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p206/r2.claim: Some exclude harmful animals and plants; advocates of the general reading answer that everything has some benefit, if only as evidence for the Maker and His oneness.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p206/r2.anchor: وقيل لا يدخل في ذلك ما فيه إيذاء من حيوان ونبات ومن قال بعموم قال : لا شيء مما على الأرض إلا وفيه جهة انتفاع

ALUSI-FULL:v15p206/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p206/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p206/r3.claim: Some restrict the adornment to particular examples: trees and rivers, flowering useful plants, animals of varied form and benefit, or precious metals and gems.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p206/r3.anchor: وقص بعضهم ما بالأشجار والأنهار وآخر بالنبات لما فيه من الأزهار المختلفة الألوان والمنافع

ALUSI-FULL:v15p206#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p206#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p206#2/r1.claim: One group restricts the adornment to greenery, water, livestock, clothes, and fruit; the author says this cannot stand as an exhaustive interpretation of a general expression.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p206#2/r1.anchor: وقالت فرقة : أريد بها الخضرة والمياه والنعم والملابس والثمار ولعمري إنه تخصيص لا يقبله الخواص

ALUSI-FULL:v15p206#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p206#2/r2.speaker: ابن جبير والحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v15p206#2/r2.claim: Ibn Jubayr and al-Hasan are reported to interpret “whatever” as men; Ibn Abbas as scholars; and Ikrima as caliphs, scholars, and emirs. The author finds a strictly rational referent unlikely and suggests examples of humans may stand for the whole by predominance.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p206#2/r2.anchor: وقيل إن ( ما ) هنا لمن يعقل والمراد بذلك على ما أخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن ابن جبير والحسن

ALUSI-FULL:v15p206#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p206#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p206#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, “whatever” includes both rational and nonrational beings, with accountable people appearing as adornment in one respect and as subjects of trial in another; 18:46 likewise calls wealth and children adornment, contrary to al-Qadi's exclusion of the tested person from the adornment.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p206#2/r3.anchor: وقد يقال : المراد بما عموم ما لا يعقل ومن يعقل فيدخل من توجه إليه التكليف وغيره

ALUSI-FULL:v15p206#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p206#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p206#2/r4.claim: If jaʿal means transformation, zīna is its second object; if it means creation, zīna is a purpose-object. The first lam modifies zīna or describes it, the second attaches to jaʿal, and the plural pronoun refers to earth's inhabitants or to the adorned things.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p206#2/r4.anchor: ونصب ( زينة ) على أنه مفعول ثان للجعل إن حمل على معنى التصيير أو على أنه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p206#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p206#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p206#2/r5.claim: Hisham ibn al-Hakam is said to permit attributing trial to God because he mistakenly thought God learns events only after they occur; Sunnis reject this and affirm God's eternal knowledge of particulars and universals.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p206#2/r5.anchor: وجوز ذلك على الله سبحانه هشام بن الحكم بناء على جهله وزعمه أنه عز وجل لا يعلم الحوادث إلا بعد وجودها

ALUSI-FULL:v15p206#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p206#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p206#2/r6.claim: Trial means God treats people as if testing them so He can reward each fittingly; the best deed is asceticism toward worldly adornment, not being deceived by it, using it lawfully, fulfilling its rights, giving thanks, and reflecting on it as a path to knowing its Maker.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p206#2/r6.anchor: وأول هذه الآية أن المراد ليعاملهم معاملة من يختبرهم ( أيهم أحسن عملا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p206#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p206#2/r7.speaker: النبي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p206#2/r7.claim: Asked by Ibn Umar which people do best, the Prophet answered: those most intelligent, most abstinent from God's prohibitions, and quickest in obedience.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p206#2/r7.anchor: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الأحسن عملا كما أخرج ذلك ابن جرير وابن أبي حاتم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p207/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207/r1.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207/r1.claim: Al-Hasan says the best in deeds are those who abandon worldly life most, and a similar view is transmitted from Sufyan al-Thawri.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207/r1.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن الحسن أنه قال : أحسنهم عملا أشدهم للدنيا تركا وأخرج نحوه عن سفيان الثوري

ALUSI-FULL:v15p207/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207/r2.claim: Other definitions rank the ascetic content with a traveler's provision highest, one who lawfully earns and spends well next, and one who gathers lawful and unlawful wealth for desires as blameworthy; the Prophet's answer is best.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207/r2.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أن الأحسن من زهد وقنع من الدنيا بزاد المسافر ووراءه وهو من استكثر من حلالها

ALUSI-FULL:v15p207/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207/r3.claim: Although the trial includes both good and bad deeds, the comparative “best” is retained because the primary aim of worldly adornment is to reveal the excellence of those who excel.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207/r3.anchor: وإيراد صيغة التفضيل مع أن الابتلاء شامل للفريقين باعتبار أعمالهم المنقسمة إلى الحسن والقبيح

ALUSI-FULL:v15p207/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207/r4.claim: Ayyuhum may be an interrogative subject with aḥsanu as predicate; the question clause is suspended from nبلو because that verb evokes inquiry or consideration.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207/r4.anchor: وأي إما إستفهامية فهي مرفوعة بالابتداء وأحسن خبرها والجملة في محل نصب بفعل الابتلاء

ALUSI-FULL:v15p207/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207/r5.claim: Alternatively, ayyuhum is a relative pronoun meaning “the one who,” built on damma and appositional to the object pronoun in nبلوهم; al-Bahr says Sibawayh permits rather than requires this construction when the relative clause's head is omitted, a point the author finds difficult.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207/r5.anchor: وإما موصولة بمعنى فهي مبنية على الضم محلها النصب على أنها بدل من ضمير النصب في ( نبلوهم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p207/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207/r6.claim: Aḥsanu remains a true comparative with its comparison omitted: God tests which people do better than those who are less good in deeds.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207/r6.anchor: والمفضل عليه محذوف والتقدير كما قال أبو حيان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p144/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p144/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p144/r7.claim: Earth's adornment is made as a test of which people do the best deeds.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p144/r7.anchor: إنا جعلنا ما على الأرض زينة لها لنبلوهم أيهم أحسن عملا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p144/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p144/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p144/r8.claim: Even snakes, scorpions, and devils count as adornment in that they point to God's oneness.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p144/r8.anchor: فإن قيل: أي: زينة في الحيات والعقارب والشياطين؟ قيل: فيها زينة على معنى أنها تدل على وحدانية الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p144/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p144/r9.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p144/r9.claim: Mujāhid says the adornment means men, who beautify the earth.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p144/r9.anchor: وقال مجاهد: أراد به الرجال خاصة وهم زينة الأرض.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p144/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p144/r10.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p144/r10.claim: Another opinion identifies the adornment with scholars and the righteous.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p144/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p144/r11.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p144/r11.claim: A further view takes it as plants, trees, and rivers, as in 10:24.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p144/r11.anchor: وقيل: الزينة بالنبات والأشجار والأنهار كما قال: "حتى إذا أخذت الأرض زخرفها وازينت"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p144#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p144#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p144#2/r1.claim: God tests people to see who acts best; another interpretation asks which person is most detached from worldly life.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p144#2/r1.anchor: {لنبلوهم} لنختبرهم {أيهم أحسن عملا} أي: أصلح عملا. وقيل: أيهم أترك للدنيا.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:7/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:7/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:7/r1.claim: What adorns the earth includes animals, plants, and minerals; it is an adornment for the earth and its inhabitants.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:7/r1.anchor: { إنا جعلنا ما على الأرض } من الحيوان والنبات والمعادن

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:7/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:7/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:7/r2.claim: The test asks who uses worldly adornment best: one not deceived, content with what suffices, and spending it properly; this also consoles the Prophet.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:7/r2.anchor: وهو من زهد فيه ولم يغتر به وقنع منه بما يزجي به أيامه

QASHANI:18:7-9/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:7-9/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:7-9/r1.claim: When people rejected the Quran, the Prophet felt his own state deficient and sought to subdue the self, out of compassion and reverence for God, blaming his own state rather than their readiness.
QASHANI:18:7-9/r1.anchor: وكان ذلك من فرط شفقته عليهم وكمال أدبه مع الله حيث أحال عدم إيمانهم

QASHANI:18:7-9/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:7-9/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:7-9/r2.claim: God consoles him: adornments on earth, including the body's self, pleasures, powers, perceptions, and desires, are a test of who best resists them for God's sake.
QASHANI:18:7-9/r2.anchor: إنا جعلنا ما على أرض البدن من النفس ولذاتها وشهواتها وقوى صفاتها وإدراكاتها

BIQAI-FULL:v4p446/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p446/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p446/r4.claim: God alone places faith in hearts; the adornment on earth comprises animals, minerals, and plants, made attractive to sight and pleasing to souls.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p446/r4.anchor: جعلنا } بما لنا من العظمة { ما على الأرض } من المواليد الثلاثة : الحيوان والمعدن والنبات { زينة لهما

BIQAI-FULL:v4p446/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p446/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p446/r5.claim: The adornment tests people by making their deeds manifest: sincere service earns reward, while using gifts only for pleasure in defiance of command merits punishment.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p446/r5.anchor: لنبلوهم } أي نعاملهم معاملة المختبر الذي يسأل لخفاء الأمر عليه بقوله تعالى : { أيهم أحسن عملا * }

BIQAI-FULL:v4p446/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p446/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p446/r6.claim: The temptation toward worldly pleasure is obvious, but the call to renounce it and infer the Creator's knowledge and power is hidden by desire.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p446/r6.anchor: ولما كان دعاء الزينة إلى حقيقة الحياة الدنيا من اللهو واللعب ظاهرا لموافقته لما طبعت عليه النفوس

BIQAI-FULL:v4p446/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p446/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p446/r7.claim: If everyone obeyed, harmful animals might lose their harm and appear as adornment; the author says this will occur in Jesus's time when children play with them.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p446/r7.anchor: والظاهر أنه لو أطاع الناس كلهم لذهبت مضرتها فبدت زينتها , كما يكون على زمن عيسى عليه السلام

QUSHAYRI:v2p208/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p208/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p208/r4.claim: Earthly adornments are visible to the eyes, while some people on earth are adornments recognized through inward insight.
QUSHAYRI:v2p208/r4.anchor: ما علىلأرض زينة لها تدرك بالأبصار ، وممن على الأرض من هو زينة لها يعرف بالأسرار

QUSHAYRI:v2p208/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p208/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p208/r5.claim: The value of a homeland comes from its inhabitants, and a dwelling is beautiful because of those who live in it.
QUSHAYRI:v2p208/r5.anchor: وإن قيمة الأوطان لقطانها ، وزينة المساكن في سكانها

QUSHAYRI:v2p208/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p208/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p208/r6.claim: God's servants adorn the world, while people of spiritual knowledge adorn Paradise.
QUSHAYRI:v2p208/r6.anchor: ويقال العباد بهم زينة الدنيا ، وأهل المعرفة بهم زينة الجنة

QUSHAYRI:v2p208/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p208/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p208/r7.claim: God's friends are the earth's adornment and a source of safety for its inhabitants.
QUSHAYRI:v2p208/r7.anchor: الأولياء زينة الأرض وهم أمان من في الأرض

QUSHAYRI:v2p208/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p208/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p208/r8.claim: When the lights of divine unity shine in monotheists' inner selves, their radiance brightens all horizons.
QUSHAYRI:v2p208/r8.anchor: إذا تلألأت أنوار التوحيد في أسرار المرحدين أشرقت جميع الآفاق بضيائهم

QUSHAYRI:v2p208/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p208/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p208/r9.claim: The best deeds are done with the truest intention and purest inward nature.
QUSHAYRI:v2p208/r9.anchor: أحسنهم عملا أصدقهم نية ، وأخلصهم طوية

QUSHAYRI:v2p208/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p208/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p208/r10.claim: Another measure of the best deed is how much its doer expects and counts on reward.

QUSHAYRI:v2p208/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p208/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p208/r11.claim: A still higher standard is to consider one's own act small and deficient beside what God deserves; the cited poem praises minimizing one's deed.
QUSHAYRI:v2p208/r11.anchor: فأحسنهم عملا أشدهم استصغارا لفعله ، وأكثرهم استحقارا لطاعته

DURR-FULL:v5p360/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p360/r5.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p360/r5.claim: The adornment of the earth is everything upon it.
DURR-FULL:v5p360/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله: {إنا جعلنا ما على الأرض زينة لها} قال: ما عليها من شيء

DURR-FULL:v5p360/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p360/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v5p360/r6.claim: The adornment of the earth is its people, meaning men.
DURR-FULL:v5p360/r6.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله: {إنا جعلنا ما على الأرض زينة لها} قال: الرجال

DURR-FULL:v5p360/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p360/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p360/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas likewise interprets the earth's adornment as men.
DURR-FULL:v5p360/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {إنا جعلنا ما على الأرض زينة لها} قال: الرجال

DURR-FULL:v5p360/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p360/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p360/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the scholars as the adornment of the earth.
DURR-FULL:v5p360/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {إنا جعلنا ما على الأرض زينة لها} قال: العلماء زينة الأرض

DURR-FULL:v5p360/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p360/r9.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v5p360/r9.claim: The adornment is men who worship God and work in obedience to Him.
DURR-FULL:v5p360/r9.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله: {إنا جعلنا ما على الأرض زينة لها} قال: هم الرجال العباد العمال لله بالطاعة

DURR-FULL:v5p360/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p360/r10.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p360/r10.claim: The Prophet explains the test as sound intellect, avoidance of God's prohibitions, and prompt obedience.
DURR-FULL:v5p360/r10.anchor: تلا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم هذه الآية {لنبلوهم أيهم أحسن عملا} فقلت: ما معنى ذلك يا رسول الله

DURR-FULL:v5p360/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p360/r11.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p360/r11.claim: The test means trial, and the best deed belongs to the person of most complete intellect.
DURR-FULL:v5p360/r11.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {لنبلوهم} قال: لنختبرهم {أيهم أحسن عملا} قال: أيهم أتم عقلا

DURR-FULL:v5p360/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p360/r12.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v5p360/r12.claim: The best deed belongs to those who most renounce worldly life.
DURR-FULL:v5p360/r12.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله: {لنبلوهم أيهم أحسن عملا} قال: أشدهم للدنيا تركا

DURR-FULL:v5p360/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p360/r13.speaker: سفيان الثوري
DURR-FULL:v5p360/r13.claim: The best deed belongs to those most ascetic toward worldly life.
DURR-FULL:v5p360/r13.anchor: عن سفيان الثوري في قوله: {لنبلوهم أيهم أحسن عملا} قال: أزهدهم في الدنيا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p496#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p496#2/r7.speaker: ابن جبير عن ابن عباس ومجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p496#2/r7.claim: They say the earth's adornment means people.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p496#2/r7.anchor: فقال ابن جبير عن ابن عباس: أراد الرجال وقاله مجاهد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p496#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p496#2/r8.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p496#2/r8.claim: ʿIkrima says adornment means caliphs, scholars, and rulers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p496#2/r8.anchor: وروى عكرمة عن ابن عباس أن الزينة الخلفاء والعلماء والأمراء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p496#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p496#2/r9.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p496#2/r9.claim: Another group says adornment is blessings, clothing, fruits, greenery, and water.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p496#2/r9.anchor: وقالت فرقة أراد النعم والملابس والثمار والخضرة والمياه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p497/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p497/r1.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p497/r1.claim: Another group takes earth's adornment generally: all things have beauty through creation and design.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p497/r1.anchor: فرقة: أراد كل ما على الأرض عموما وليس شيء إلا وفيه زينة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p497/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p497/r2.speaker: رسول الله
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p497/r2.claim: A Prophetic report calls the world lush and sweet, says God makes people successors to test them, and warns about the world and women.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p497/r2.anchor: الدنيا خضرة حلوة وإن الله مستخلفكم فيها فناظر كيف تعملون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p497/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p497/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p497/r3.claim: Zīnata can be the second object of jaʿalnā or its purpose, depending on the verb's meaning.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p497/r3.anchor: وزينة مفعول ثان أو مفعول من أجله بحسب معنى «جعل»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p497/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p497/r4.speaker: سفيان الثوري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p497/r4.claim: Sufyān al-Thawrī says the best deeds belong to those most ascetic toward the world.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p497/r4.anchor: قال سفيان الثوري: «أحسنهم عملا» أزهدهم فيها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p497/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p497/r5.speaker: أبو عاصم العسقلاني
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p497/r5.claim: Abū ʿĀṣim says the best act is to leave the world behind.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p497/r5.anchor: وقال أبو عاصم العسقلاني: أحسن عملا: أترك لها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p497/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p497/r6.speaker: أبو محمد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p497/r6.claim: The author's father defines good work as taking what is due and spending rightly, with faith, obligations, avoiding prohibitions, and recommended deeds.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p497/r6.anchor: وكان أبي رضي الله عنه يقول: أحسن العمل أخذ بحق واتفاق في حق

SULAMI:v1p401#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p401#2/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p401#2/r1.claim: The best deed is the best turning away from worldly adornment and relinquishment of it.
SULAMI:v1p401#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : لنبلوهم أيهم أحسن عملا ، أحسن إعراضا عنها وتركا لها

SULAMI:v1p401#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p401#2/r2.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v1p401#2/r2.claim: The best deed is trusting God most fully in the world.
SULAMI:v1p401#2/r2.anchor: وقال سهل : أيهم أحسن توكلا علينا فيها

SULAMI:v1p401#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p401#2/r3.speaker: أبو علي الروذباري
SULAMI:v1p401#2/r3.claim: Once people knew God personally manages affairs, the wise recognized their true condition, disdained the world, became content, and turned away from it.
SULAMI:v1p401#2/r3.anchor: قال أبو علي الروذباري : إن القوم لما أيقنوا أن الله تولى الأمور بنفسه عرف كل عاقل حقيقة ما هم فيه

SULAMI:v1p401#2/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p401#2/r4.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p401#2/r4.claim: The best deed is affirming servanthood in word and action.
SULAMI:v1p401#2/r4.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : أيهم أقر بالعبودية قولا وفعلا

SULAMI:v1p401#2/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p401#2/r5.speaker: فارس
SULAMI:v1p401#2/r5.claim: Good work is truthful, purposeful, and well intentioned.
SULAMI:v1p401#2/r5.anchor: وقال فارس في قوله : أيهم أحسن عملا . قال : صدقا وقصدا ونية

SULAMI:v1p401#2/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p401#2/r6.speaker: القاسم
SULAMI:v1p401#2/r6.claim: Good work belongs to the person with the emptiest heart, keenest perception, and best-guided comportment.
SULAMI:v1p401#2/r6.anchor: وقال القاسم : أفرغ قلبا وأحسن فطنة وأهدى سمتا

SULAMI:v1p401#2/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p401#2/r7.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p401#2/r7.claim: Good work is the agent's forgetting both self and deed, and being annihilated in the Real for the Real.
SULAMI:v1p401#2/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم : حسن العمل نسيان العامل نفسه ، وعمله والفناء بالحق للحق

SULAMI:v1p401#2/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p401#2/r8.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p401#2/r8.claim: Good work means refraining from beautifying oneself with one's deeds.
SULAMI:v1p401#2/r8.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمه الله : وعليهم حسن العمل ترك التزين به

SULAMI:v1p401#2/r9.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p401#2/r9.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v1p401#2/r9.claim: Good work is steadfastness upon the Sunnah.
SULAMI:v1p401#2/r9.anchor: وقال سهل : حسن العمل الاستقامة عليه بالسنة

SULAMI:v1p401#2/r10.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p401#2/r10.speaker: القاسم
SULAMI:v1p401#2/r10.claim: The adornments of the earth are the prophets, saints, godly scholars, and spiritual pillars.
SULAMI:v1p401#2/r10.anchor: قال القاسم : زينة الأرض الأنبياء والأولياء والعلماء الربانيون والأوتاد

SULAMI:v1p401#2/r11.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p401#2/r11.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p401#2/r11.claim: Those who know and love God and long for Him are the world's adornment, stars, moons, and suns.
SULAMI:v1p401#2/r11.anchor: وقيل : أهل المعرفة بالله ، والمحبة له ، والمشتاقون إليه هم زينة الأرض ونجومها وأقمارها

SULAMI:v1p401#2/r12.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p401#2/r12.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v1p401#2/r12.claim: The best workers turn away from and avoid the world.
SULAMI:v1p401#2/r12.anchor: قال سهل : إنهم أحسن عملا عنها أعراضا واجتنابا

SULAMI:v1p401#2/r13.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p401#2/r13.speaker: الحسين
SULAMI:v1p401#2/r13.claim: The earth's adornment is devout people who serve God through obedience, and the best deed is leaving the world most completely.
SULAMI:v1p401#2/r13.anchor: وعن الحسين في قوله : ﴿ إنا جعلنا ما على الأرض زينة لها ﴾ قال : هم الرجال العباد العمال لله بالطاعة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p105#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p105#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p105#2/r1.claim: The adornment on earth may be people, reported by Saʿid ibn Jubayr from Ibn Abbas.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p105#2/r1.anchor: أنهم الرجال رواه سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p105#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p105#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p105#2/r2.claim: Another Ibn Abbas view, reported by Mujahid, identifies the adornment as scholars.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p105#2/r2.anchor: العلماء رواه مجاهد عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p105#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p105#2/r3.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p105#2/r3.claim: On the people-or-scholars readings, mā is an indefinite expression functioning in place of man, according to Ibn al-Anbari.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p105#2/r3.anchor: فعلى هذين القولين تكون ما في موضع من لأنها في موضع إبهام قاله ابن الانباري

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p105#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p105#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p105#2/r4.claim: Mujahid’s broad view is that the adornment is everything on earth, including plants, water, and minerals.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p105#2/r4.anchor: أنه ما عليها من شيء قاله مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p105#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p105#2/r5.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p105#2/r5.claim: A fourth view identifies the adornment as vegetation and trees.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p105#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p105#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p105#2/r6.claim: Mujahid’s universal reading is the broadest because it includes vegetation, water, minerals, and other earthly things.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p105#2/r6.anchor: وقول مجاهد أعم يدخل فيه النبات والماء والمعادن وغير ذلك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p105#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p105#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p105#2/r7.claim: Ugly things can be called adornment by general wording for some things; people and scholars adorn through worship or pointing to their Creator, plants are earth’s covering and jewelry, and everything adorns it by pointing to its Maker.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p105#2/r7.anchor: فلكونه دالا على خالقه فكأنه زينة الأرض من هذه الجهة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p105#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p105#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p105#2/r8.claim: Testing means dealing with creation as one who tests, to reveal which person does the best work.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p105#2/r8.anchor: أي لنختبر الخلق والمعنى لنعاملهم معاملة المبتلى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p105#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p105#2/r9.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p105#2/r9.claim: If the adornment means plants, the pronoun refers to earth’s inhabitants who see them; if it means people, it refers back to mā as a collective.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p105#2/r9.anchor: من قال إن ما على الأرض يعني به النبات قال الهاء والميم ترجع إلى سكان الأرض

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p105#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p105#2/r10.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p105#2/r10.claim: Al-Hasan says the best deed is greater asceticism toward worldly life.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p105#2/r10.anchor: قال الحسن أيهم أزهد في الدنيا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p105#2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p105#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p105#2/r11.claim: The author previously discussed four views on this verse at 11:7.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p105#2/r11.anchor: وقد ذكرنا في هذه الآية أربعة أقوال في سورة هود

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p137/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p137/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p137/r6.claim: The world is a transient abode decorated with vanishing adornment and made a place of testing, not permanent residence, to reveal who does best in deeds.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p137/r6.anchor: ثم أخبر تعالى أنه جعل الدنيا دارا فانية مزينة بزينة زائلة. وإنما جعلها دار اختبار لا دار قرار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p137/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p137/r7.speaker: أبو سعيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p137/r7.claim: The Prophet likens worldly life to something green and sweet, says God appoints people as successors to see how they act, and warns against worldly life and women, whose temptation first tested Israel.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p137/r7.anchor: قال قتادة، عن أبي نضرة، عن أبي سعيد، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:

TUSTARI:18:7/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:18:7/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:18:7/r1.claim: The best deed is greater withdrawal from worldly distractions, with humility, stillness toward God, trust in Him, and turning toward Him.
TUSTARI:18:7/r1.anchor: قال: أيهم أحسن إعراضا عن الدنيا، وما يوجب الاشتغال عن الله تعالى، وإخباتا وسكونا إلينا،

JISHUMI:v6p4344/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4344/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4344/r5.claim: Ṣaʿīd means soil or the earth’s surface; it can also mean level ground.
JISHUMI:v6p4344/r5.anchor: الصعيد: التراب، وقيل: الصعيد: وجه الأرض، والصعيد الأرض المستوية.

JISHUMI:v6p4344/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4344/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4344/r8.claim: أيهم is nominative as a new subject because what precedes an interrogative does not govern what follows; 18:12 offers a parallel.
JISHUMI:v6p4344/r8.anchor: أيهم رفع على الابتداء لأن ما قبل حرف الاستفهام لا يعمل فيما بعده، ومثله: (أي الحزبين أحصى لما لبثوا).

JISHUMI:v6p4344/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4344/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4344/r10.claim: The adornments include trees, fruits, precious metals, vessels, animals, livestock, and useful things.
JISHUMI:v6p4344/r10.anchor: قيل: هي الأشجار، والثمار، والذهب، والفضة، والأواني، والدواب، والمواشي، وسائر ما ينتفع به،

JISHUMI:v6p4344/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4344/r11.speaker: الضحاك
JISHUMI:v6p4344/r11.claim: Another view says the adornment means people in particular.
JISHUMI:v6p4344/r11.anchor: وقيل: أراد به الرجال خاصة، عن الضحاك.

JISHUMI:v6p4344/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4344/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4344/r12.claim: God tests people through blessings to distinguish the grateful from the unbelieving, although He already knows their outcomes.
JISHUMI:v6p4344/r12.anchor: والله تعالى كلفهم ليظهر الشاكر من الكافر وإن كان عالما بما يؤول إليه حالهم.

JISHUMI:v6p4344/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4344/r13.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v6p4344/r13.claim: Desire makes adornment a test; its prohibited use must be avoided and earns reward, while committing it earns punishment.
JISHUMI:v6p4344/r13.anchor: لأن الشهوة تتعلق بها، ولا يصح التكليف إلا بها وفيها حرام يجب الامتناع منه، وإذا امتنع وجب الثواب،

JISHUMI:v6p4344/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4344/r14.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v6p4344/r14.claim: Permissible adornments require gratitude and spending in proper ways.
JISHUMI:v6p4344/r14.anchor: وفيها الحلال يجب الشكر عليه وإنفاقه في مواضعه، عن أبي مسلم.

JISHUMI:v6p4345/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4345/r1.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v6p4345/r1.claim: Another view makes the test whether people use adornment in obedience rather than disobedience.
JISHUMI:v6p4345/r1.anchor: وقيل: الابتلاء فيه أن تستعمل تلك الزينة في طاعته دون معاصيه، عن أبي علي.

JISHUMI:v6p4345/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4345/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4345/r2.claim: The test reveals deeds already known to God so recompense matches them; the best are most obedient.
JISHUMI:v6p4345/r2.anchor: أيهم أحسن عملا أي: ليظهر منهم ما كان معلوما ليكون الجزاء على قدر العمل والأحسن عملا الأعمل بطاعة الله

JISHUMI:v6p4345/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4345/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4345/r3.claim: Another definition of the best work is steadfastness upon the Sunna.
JISHUMI:v6p4345/r3.anchor: وقيل: حسن العمل: الاستقامة على السنة

JISHUMI:v6p4345/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4345/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4345/r8.claim: The earth’s contents are adornment and great blessings, created as the setting for moral responsibility.
JISHUMI:v6p4345/r8.anchor: تدل الآية على أن جميع ما في الأرض زينة لها، وعلى عظيم نعم الله على الخلق بها.

JISHUMI:v6p4345/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4345/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4345/r9.claim: The adornment was created for moral responsibility and testing.
JISHUMI:v6p4345/r9.anchor: وتدل على أنه فعل ذلك لمكان التكليف.

JISHUMI:v6p4345/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4345/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4345/r10.claim: God intends people to do good, as shown by asking which of them will act best.
JISHUMI:v6p4345/r10.anchor: وتدل على أنه أراد منهم العمل الصالح لولا ذلك لما قال: (أيهم أحسن عملا).

JISHUMI:v6p4345/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4345/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4345/r12.claim: Testing presupposes human deeds that originate with people, refuting compulsion.
JISHUMI:v6p4345/r12.anchor: ويدل قوله: (أحسن عملا) أن أفعالهم حادثة من جهتهم، لولا ذلك لما صح الابتلاء

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r1.speaker: مقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r1.claim: The earth’s adornment means its trees and rivers.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r1.anchor: أحدها : أنها الأشجار والأنهار التي زين الله الأرض بها , قاله مقاتل .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r2.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r2.claim: The adornment is humanity, since people beautify the earth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r2.anchor: الثاني : أنهم الرجال لأنهم زينة الأرض , قاله الكلبي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r3.speaker: القاسم
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r3.claim: The adornment is the prophets and scholars.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r3.anchor: الثالث : أنهم الأنبياء والعلماء , قاله القاسم .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r4.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r4.claim: Everything on earth counts as its adornment.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r4.anchor: الرابع : أن كل ما على الأرض زينة لها , قاله مجاهد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r5.claim: Alternatively, the adornments are desires that appear attractive to the people who live there.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r5.anchor: الخامس : أن معنى { زينة لها } أي شهوات لأهلها تزين في أعينهم وأنفسهم .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r6.speaker: ابن عطاء
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r6.claim: The test asks who best turns away from and abandons worldly adornment.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r6.anchor: أحدها : أيهم أحسن إعراضا عنها وتركا لها , قاله ابن عطاء .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r7.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r7.claim: The test asks who trusts God best with worldly adornment.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r7.anchor: الثاني : أيهم أحسن توكلا علينا فيها , قاله سهل بن عبد الله .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r8.claim: The test may ask whose heart is purest and conduct most rightly guided.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r8.anchor: الثالث : أيهم أصفى قلبا وأهدى سمتا .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r9.claim: Alternatively, the test asks who draws the most lessons from worldly adornment.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r9.anchor: ويحتمل رابعا : لنختبرهم أيهم أكثر اعتبارا بها .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r10.claim: Alternatively, the test concerns who best avoids what is unlawful among worldly things.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r10.anchor: ويحتمل خامسا : لنختبرهم في تجافي الحرام منها .

MUJAHID:v1p373#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p373#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p373#2/r1.claim: Mujahid explains the earth's adornment as everything upon it.
MUJAHID:v1p373#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ إنا جعلنا ما على الأرض زينة لها ﴾ يعني ما عليها من شيء

MUQATIL:18:6-8/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:6-8/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:6-8/r2.claim: Earth's vegetation renewed year by year is its adornment and a test of who acts best.
MUQATIL:18:6-8/r2.anchor: { إنا جعلنا ما على الأرض } من النبت عاما بعام، { زينة لها لنبلوهم } ، يعني لنختبرهم، { أيهم أحسن عملا }

NASAFI-FULL:v3p4#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p4#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p4#2/r1.claim: The earth’s adornment comprises worldly luxuries and whatever people find pleasing; it is made a test of who acts best.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p4#2/r1.anchor: أي ما يصلح أن يكوو زينة لها ولأهلها من زخارف الدنيا وما يستحسن منها

NASAFI-FULL:v3p4#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p4#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p4#2/r2.claim: The best action is renouncing worldly attachment and refusing to be deceived by it.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p4#2/r2.anchor: وحسن العمل الزهد فيها وترك الاغترار بها

QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3/r10.speaker: ابن إسحاق
QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3/r10.claim: Ibn Ishaq explains the trial as testing who follows God's command and obeys Him best.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3/r10.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق: أي أيهم أتبع لأمري وأعمل بطاعتي.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:7/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7/r1.claim: Grammatically, ma and zinatan are both direct objects; everything on earth can be an adornment because it points to its Creator.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7/r1.anchor: مفعولان. والزينة كل ما على وجه الأرض فهو عموم لأنه دال على بارئه.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:7/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7/r2.speaker: ابن جبير عن ابن عباس ومجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7/r2.claim: One interpretation identifies the adornment as people; the report is given through Ibn Jubayr from Ibn Abbas and attributed to Mujahid.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7/r2.anchor: وقال ابن جبير عن ابن عباس: أراد بالزينة الرجال قال مجاهد.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:7/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7/r3.speaker: ابن عباس عن عكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7/r3.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas through Ikrima identifies the adornment as rulers and leaders.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7/r3.anchor: وروى عكرمة عن ابن عباس أن الزينة الخلفاء والأمراء

QURTUBI-FULL:18:7/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7/r4.speaker: ابن عباس عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7/r4.claim: A report through Ibn Abi Najih from Mujahid says the earth's adornment is its scholars.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7/r4.anchor: وروى ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد عن ابن عباس في قوله تعالى: «إنا جعلنا ما على الأرض زينة لها» قال: العلماء زينة الأرض.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:7/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7/r5.speaker: فرقة
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7/r5.claim: Another group narrows the adornment to blessings, clothing, fruit, greenery, water, and similar things, excluding bare mountains and harmful creatures.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7/r5.anchor: وقالت فرقة: أراد النعم والملابس والثمار والخضرة والمياه، ونحو هذا

QURTUBI-FULL:18:7/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7/r6.claim: Al-Qurtubi prefers the general meaning: everything on earth is an adornment through its creation, craftsmanship, and perfection.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7/r6.anchor: والقول بالعموم أولى، وأن كل ما على الأرض فيه زينة من جهة خلقه وصنعه وإحكامه.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:7/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7/r7.claim: The verse consoles Muhammad: earthly display is a test of who reflects and believes and who rejects, to be repaid at resurrection, so he should not be distressed by unbelief.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7/r7.anchor: والآية بسط في التسلية أي لا تهتم يا محمد للدنيا وأهلها فإنا إنما جعلنا ذلك امتحانا

QURTUBI-FULL:18:7/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7/r8.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7/r8.claim: Two reports from Abu Said al-Khudri compare worldly life to fresh, sweet growth and warn of the dangers in its blossoms and blessings; Muslim transmits them.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7/r8.anchor: إن الدنيا خضرة حلوة والله مستخلفكم فيها فينظر كيف تعملون

QURTUBI-FULL:18:7/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7/r9.claim: The world is delicious to taste and pleasing to see, like attractive fruit; God tests which people do the best deeds, and only His help lets them resist what He has adorned.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7/r9.anchor: والمعنى: أن الدنيا مستطابة في ذوقها معجبة في منظرها كالثمر المستحلى

QURTUBI-FULL:18:7/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7/r10.speaker: عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7/r10.claim: Umar prayed for help to spend rightly what God had adorned, acknowledging that people naturally rejoice in it.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7/r10.anchor: اللهم إنا لا نستطيع إلا أن نفرح بما زينته لنا

QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r1.claim: The Prophet compared greedy acquisition of worldly goods to someone who eats without becoming full; those consumed by accumulation face temptation and little safety, while success belongs to the contented person with sufficient provision.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r1.anchor: فمن أخذه بطيب نفس بورك له فيه ومن أخذه بإشراف نفس كان

QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r2.speaker: أبو ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r2.claim: Ibn Atiyya's father defines the best deed as lawful acquisition and spending, faith, fulfilling obligations, avoiding prohibitions, and doing abundant recommended acts.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r2.anchor: كان أبي رضي الله عنه يقول في قوله: «أحسن عملا» أحسن العمل أخذ بحق وإنفاق في حق

QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r3.claim: Al-Qurtubi praises that concise definition and says the Prophet summarized it to Sufyan ibn Abd Allah: believe in God and remain upright.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r3.anchor:
آمنت بالله ثم استقم "
خرجه مسلم.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r4.speaker: سفيان الثوري
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r4.claim: Al-Thawri glosses the best deed as being most ascetic toward worldly life.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r4.anchor: وقال سفيان الثوري: «أحسن عملا» أزهدهم فيها.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r5.speaker: أبو عصام العسقلاني
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r5.claim: Abu Asim al-Asqalani glosses the best deed as leaving worldly life most completely.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r5.anchor: وكذلك قال أبو عصام العسقلاني: «أحسن عملا» أترك لها.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r6.speaker: سفيان الثوري
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r6.claim: One definition of asceticism is short hopes, not necessarily eating coarse food or wearing a rough cloak; al-Qurtubi says this makes one content with what suffices.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r6.anchor: قصر الأمل وليس بأكل الخشن ولبس العباء قاله سفيان الثوري

QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r7.speaker: الأوزاعي
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r7.claim: Al-Awzai's view defines asceticism as disliking commendation and praise.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r7.anchor: وقال قوم: بغض المحمدة وحب الثناء. وهو قول الأوزاعي

QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r8.speaker: فضيل
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r8.claim: Al-Fudayl's view says asceticism is abandoning the whole world, whether one likes or dislikes doing so.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r8.anchor: وقال قوم: ترك الدنيا كلها هو الزهد أحب تركها أم كره. وهو قول فضيل.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r9.speaker: بشر بن الحارث
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r9.claim: Bishr ibn al-Harith says love of the world means love of meeting people, while asceticism means avoiding meeting them; al-Fudayl also calls withdrawal from people a sign of asceticism.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r9.anchor: وعن بشر بن الحارث قال: حب الدنيا حب لقاء الناس، والزهد في الدنيا الزهد في لقاء الناس.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r10.speaker: إبراهيم بن أدهم
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r10.claim: Ibrahim ibn Adham says one is not truly ascetic until leaving the world is more beloved than acquiring it.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r10.anchor: لا يكون الزاهد زاهدا حتى يكون ترك الدنيا أحب إليه من أخذها قاله إبراهيم بن أدهم

QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r11.speaker: ابن المبارك
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r11.claim: Ibn al-Mubarak defines asceticism as renunciation in the heart.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r11.anchor: وقال قوم: الزهد أن تزهد في الدنيا بقلبك قاله ابن المبارك.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r12.speaker: فرقة
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r12.claim: Another group identifies asceticism with loving death.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r13.claim: Al-Qurtubi prefers the first definition because it encompasses the substance of the other definitions.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:7#2/r13.anchor: والقول الأول يعم هذه الأقوال بالمعنى فهو أولى

RAZI-FULL:v21p67#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p67#3/r1.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v21p67#3/r1.claim: God adorned the earth with benefits to test people through duties yet continues providing for disbelievers; likewise Muhammad should keep calling them despite grief.
RAZI-FULL:v21p67#3/r1.anchor: خلقت الأرض وزينتها وأخرجت منها أنواع المنافع والمصالح

RAZI-FULL:v21p67#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p67#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p67#3/r2.claim: Reported interpretations range from plants and trees to the addition of minerals, gold, and silver.
RAZI-FULL:v21p67#3/r2.anchor: فقال بعضهم النبات والشجر وضم بعضهم إليه الذهب والفضة والمعادن

RAZI-FULL:v21p67#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p67#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p67#3/r3.claim: Another interpretation includes the other animals, and another takes people themselves as earth's adornment.

RAZI-FULL:v21p67#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p67#3/r4.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v21p67#3/r4.claim: Some identify people themselves as the adornment of the earth.
RAZI-FULL:v21p67#3/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم بل المراد الناس فهم زينة الأرض

RAZI-FULL:v21p67#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p67#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p67#3/r5.claim: The earthly kinds are minerals, plants, and animals, with humans the noblest animals.
RAZI-FULL:v21p67#3/r5.anchor: فليس بالأرض إلا المواليد الثلاثة وهي المعادن والنبات والحيوان

RAZI-FULL:v21p67#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p67#3/r6.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v21p67#3/r6.claim: Al-Qadi excludes morally responsible humans from the adornment because they are the ones being tested, while plants and animals are included as useful things.
RAZI-FULL:v21p67#3/r6.anchor: وقال القاضي : الأولى أنه لا يدخل في هذه الزينة المكلف

RAZI-FULL:v21p67#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p67#3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p67#3/r7.claim: ‘Adornment for it’ means adornment for the earth; what beautifies the earth may be called its adornment, just as stars adorn the sky.
RAZI-FULL:v21p67#3/r7.anchor: أي للأرض ولا يمتنع أن يكون ما يحسن به الأرض زينة للأرض

RAZI-FULL:v21p67#3/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p67#3/r8.speaker: هشام بن الحكم
RAZI-FULL:v21p67#3/r8.claim: Hisham says God learns events only when they occur; otherwise foreknown outcomes would remove divine and human ability to act otherwise, so testing is literal.
RAZI-FULL:v21p67#3/r8.anchor: ذهب هشام بن الحكم إلى أنه تعالى لا يعلم الحوادث إلا عند دخولها في الوجود

RAZI-FULL:v21p67#3/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p67#3/r9.speaker: جمهور علماء الإسلام
RAZI-FULL:v21p67#3/r9.claim: The majority hold that God eternally knows every particular; testing language means treating people as an examiner would, not learning from them.
RAZI-FULL:v21p67#3/r9.anchor: جمهور علماء الإسلام فقد استبعدوا هذا القول وقالوا : إنه تعالى من الأزل إلى الأبد

RAZI-FULL:v21p68/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p68/r1.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v21p68/r1.claim: Testing means making manifest who is most obedient and constant in worship and will attain Paradise; God imposed duties so people obey, refuting the claim that some were created for Hell.
RAZI-FULL:v21p68/r1.anchor: يبلوهم ليبصرهم أيهم أطوع لله وأشد استمرارا على خدمته

RAZI-FULL:v21p68/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p68/r2.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v21p68/r2.claim: The purpose-connoting lām supports the Mu'tazilite claim that God's acts are directed toward ends.
RAZI-FULL:v21p68/r2.anchor: تدل ظاهرا على أن أفعال الله معللة بالأغراض عند المعتزلة

RAZI-FULL:v21p68/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p68/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p68/r3.claim: Al-Razi's school rejects divine acts being caused by purposes: needing an intermediary to obtain a purpose implies incapacity, impossible for God.
RAZI-FULL:v21p68/r3.anchor: التعليل بالغرض إنما يصح في حق من لا يمكنه تحصيل ذلك الغرض

RAZI-FULL:v21p68/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p68/r4.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v21p68/r4.claim: Ayyuhum is nominative as the subject despite its interrogative form; the sense is to test who acts best.
RAZI-FULL:v21p68/r4.anchor: قال الزجاج : أيهم رفع بالإبتداء إلا أن لفظه لفظ الاستفهام

STUDYQURAN:18:7/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:7/r1.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:18:7/r1.claim: Earth’s adornment includes its plants, animals, gold, and metals; al-Rāzī considers humanity its noblest creature.
STUDYQURAN:18:7/r1.anchor: The earth is “adorned” by the various phenomena found upon it or in it, including its flora and fauna and its precious gold and metals

STUDYQURAN:18:7/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:7/r2.speaker: Abū Ḥāmid al-Ghazzālī
STUDYQURAN:18:7/r2.claim: Earthly adornment tests whether people maintain detachment and asceticism toward the world.
STUDYQURAN:18:7/r2.anchor: the “adornment” of the earth is a means by which God tries human beings with regard to their ability to maintain an attitude of detachment and asceticism toward the world

NAHHAS:v2p447/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p447/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p447/r9.claim: One analysis makes ما and زينة two objects; one reading restricts them to trees, fruit, wealth, and similar things, while another makes them universal because they point to their Creator.
NAHHAS:v2p447/r9.anchor: قيل ' ما ' و ' زينة ' مفعولان ويكون فيه تقديران

NAHHAS:v2p447/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p447/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p447/r10.claim: Another analysis takes جعلنا as ‘created,’ with ما as its object and زينة as a purpose object; Abū Jaʿfar calls this a good view.
NAHHAS:v2p447/r10.anchor: وقول آخر أن جعلنا ههنا بمعنى خلقنا يتعدى إلى ' ما ' و ' زينة ' مفعول من أجله ، وهذا قول حسن

NAHHAS:v2p447/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p447/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p447/r11.claim: God tests people by commanding obedience to see who acts best; the best deed is one that renounces worldly adornment.
NAHHAS:v2p447/r11.anchor: ^ ( لنبلوهم ) أي لنختبرهم فنأمرهم بالطاعة لننظر ^ ( أيهم أحسن عملا ) ^

TAB-FULL:v15p152/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p152/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p152/r1.claim: Mujahid says the adornment includes everything on earth.
TAB-FULL:v15p152/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، { ما على الأرض زينة لها} [الكهف: 7] قال: ما عليها من شيء

TAB-FULL:v15p152/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p152/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p152/r2.claim: Qatada transmits the Prophet’s saying that the world is green and sweet, God makes people successors in it to see how they act, and they should beware the world and women.
TAB-FULL:v15p152/r2.anchor: عن قتادة قوله: {إنا جعلنا ما على الأرض زينة لها} [الكهف: 7] ذكر لنا أن نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقول

TAB-FULL:v15p153/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p153/r1.speaker: أبو عاصم العسقلاني
TAB-FULL:v15p153/r1.claim: Abu Asim al-Asqalani says the best in deeds is whoever abandons the world’s adornment most.
TAB-FULL:v15p153/r1.anchor: ثنا أبو عاصم العسقلاني، قال: {لنبلوهم أيهم أحسن عملا} [الكهف: 7] قال: أترك لها

TAB-FULL:v15p153/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p153/r2.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v15p153/r2.claim: Ibn Ishaq explains the test as determining who most follows God’s command and works in obedience.
TAB-FULL:v15p153/r2.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، {إنا جعلنا ما على الأرض زينة لها لنبلوهم أيهم أحسن عملا} [الكهف: 7] اختبارا لهم أيهم أتبع لأمري وأعمل بطاعتي

TABATABAI:18:6-7/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:6-7/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:6-7/r3.claim: Earth's adornments are attractive goods, children, status, and other attachments; God uses them to draw lofty human souls into earthly life for a test, then removes their beauty and attachments when the term ends, leaving people alone for judgment.
TABATABAI:18:6-7/r3.anchor: فكان ما على الأرض وهو جميل عندهم محبوب في أنفسهم زينة للأرض وحليه تتحلى بها لكونه عليها

TABATABAI:18:8/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:8/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:18:8/r8.claim: Al-Durr al-Manthūr reports from Ibn ʿUmar that the Prophet defines the best deed as greatest understanding, strongest restraint from God's prohibitions, and quickest obedience.
TABATABAI:18:8/r8.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال تلا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم هذه الآية { لنبلوهم أيهم أحسن عملا }

TABRISI:18:7-8/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:7-8/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:7-8/r1.claim: Ṣaʿīd is the earth's surface; al-Zajjāj also glosses it as a plantless road. Juruz is barren land, imagined to consume plants.
TABRISI:18:7-8/r1.anchor: الصعيد ظهر الأرض وقال الزجاج الصعيد الطريق الذي لا نبات به والجرز الأرض التي لا تنبت

TABRISI:18:7-8/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:7-8/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:7-8/r2.claim: Arabic describes land as jaraz or ajrāz and a drought year as al-jazar; a rajaz line witnesses the term.
TABRISI:18:7-8/r2.anchor: ويقال للسنة المجدبة الجزر لجدوبها ويبسها وقلة أمطارها

TABRISI:18:7-8/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:7-8/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:7-8/r3.claim: Ayyuhum is nominative as the subject because it is an interrogative with initial position; the testing clause suspends the verb in the sense of knowing which person acts best.
TABRISI:18:7-8/r3.anchor: أيهم مرفوع بالابتداء لأن لفظه لفظ الاستفهام والاستفهام له صدر الكلام

TABRISI:18:7-8/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:7-8/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:7-8/r4.claim: The earth's adornment includes rivers, trees, and kinds of created things: inanimate, animal, and plant life.
TABRISI:18:7-8/r4.anchor: من الأنهار والأشجار وأنواع المخلوقات من الجماد والحيوان والنبات

TABRISI:18:7-8/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:7-8/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:7-8/r5.claim: God tests people to expose who acts best, meaning most productively in obedience and most obedient to Him.
TABRISI:18:7-8/r5.anchor: الأحسن عملا الأعمل بطاعة الله والأطوع له

TABRISI:18:7-8/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:7-8/r6.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:18:7-8/r6.claim: Testing means commands and prohibitions through which the obedient and disobedient become evident.
TABRISI:18:7-8/r6.anchor: معنى الابتلاء الأمر والنهي لأن بهما يظهر المطيع من العاصي

TABRISI:18:7-8/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:7-8/r7.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:18:7-8/r7.claim: The adornment of the earth may mean its men, or its prophets and scholars.
TABRISI:18:7-8/r7.anchor: أراد بالزينة الرجال لأنهم زينة الأرض

TABRISI:18:7-8/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:7-8/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:7-8/r10.claim: The verse implies God wills righteous action and human acts originate from people; otherwise testing would be invalid, refuting the determinists.
TABRISI:18:7-8/r10.anchor: وفي قوله أيهم أحسن عملا دلالة على أنه سبحانه أراد من الخلق العمل الصالح

THALABI:v6p144#4/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p144#4/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p144#4/r7.claim: Everything on earth is its adornment; al-Dahhak narrows this to flourishing plants, and the trial asks who is most ascetic toward it.
THALABI:v6p144#4/r7.anchor: إنا جعلنا ما على الأرض من كل شيء زينة لها، قال الضحاك من الزاكية خاصة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p528/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p528/r1.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p528/r1.claim: The adornment on earth includes the seas, mountains, trees, and plants.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p528/r1.anchor: قال مجاهد: (ما عليها من شيء من البحار، والجبال، والأشجار، والنبات)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p528#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p528#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p528#2/r1.claim: God adorned the earth with water, minerals, living creatures, and inanimate things; this covers all that is on it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p528#2/r1.anchor: إنا زينا الأرض بما خلقنا فيها من الماء، والمعادن، وأنواع المخلوقات،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p528#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p528#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p528#2/r2.claim: The trial tests God's creatures through what they can understand.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p528#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد الاختبار في خلقه بما يفهمون)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p528#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p528#2/r3.speaker: الحسن وأبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p528#2/r3.claim: The best deed is that of the person who is most ascetic toward the adornments of worldly life.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p528#2/r3.anchor: قال الحسن: (أيهم أزهد في الدنيا زهدا، وأترك لها تركا)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p528#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p528#2/r4.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p528#2/r4.claim: He takes the best deed to mean making the best use of the wealth one has been given.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p528#2/r4.anchor: وقال مقاتل: (أيهم أصلح فيما أوتي من المال)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p528#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p528#2/r5.speaker: قتادة عن النبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p528#2/r5.claim: The Prophet likened the world to something green and sweet, said God made people successors in it to see how they act, and warned them against its temptation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p528#2/r5.anchor: إن الدنيا خضرة حلوة، # وإن الله مستخلفكم فيها فناظر كيف تعملون،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p528#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p528#2/r6.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p528#2/r6.claim: Ayyuhum is nominative as a subject because it has the form of an interrogative; the meaning asks which person is better.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p528#2/r6.anchor: قال الزجاج: (و {أيهم} رفع بالابتداء؛ لأن لفظه لفظ الاستفهام)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p528#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p528#2/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p528#2/r7.claim: God will destroy all the earth's adornments, as the next verse says.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p528#2/r7.anchor: ثم أعلم جل وعز أنه [مبيد] (¬3) ومفن ذلك كله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:6-9/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:6-9/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:6-9/r3.claim: The adornment of the earth includes its trees, vegetation, water, and every living thing; God created these as its decoration.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:6-9/r3.anchor: من الأشجار والنبات ولاماء وكل ذي روح على الأرض

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:6-9/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:6-9/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:6-9/r4.claim: Being best in deeds means being most detached from worldly adornment and leaving it behind.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:6-9/r4.anchor: { لنبلوهم أيهم أحسن عملا } أزهد فيها، وأترك لها، ثم أعلم أنه يفني ذلك كله

ELMALILI:18:7-8/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:18:7-8/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:18:7-8/r1.claim: God made earthly adornments a trial for believers and unbelievers, manifesting through their deeds who acts best, then rewarding good and punishing evil.
ELMALILI:18:7-8/r1.anchor: mü’min ve gayr-i mü’min insanları mübtelâ kılalım, hangisi amelen daha güzel imtihan edelim

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:6/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:6/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:6/r2.claim: God made worldly adornments such as wealth, property, children, and riches attractive as a test of who acts best; people have will, moral discernment, and accountability, without which testing would be meaningless.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:6/r2.anchor: Allah Teâlâ, kimlerin daha iyi davranışlarda bulunacağını denemek için bunca güzel nimetleri; malı, mülkü, evlât ve serveti, dünyanın bir süsü olarak yaratıp çekici kılmıştır.

SAMIN-DURR:18:7/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:7/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:7/r1.claim: Zīna may be accusative of purpose, circumstantial if jaʿalnā means ‘created,’ or a second object if it means ‘made’; li-hā may express purpose with zīna, be an extra lām, or modify an omitted adjective of zīna.
SAMIN-DURR:18:7/r1.anchor: أن ينتصب على المفعول له، وأن يتنصب على الحال إن جعلت

SAMIN-DURR:18:7/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:7/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:7/r2.claim: Linabluwهم is attached to jaʿalnā under either of its meanings, ‘created’ or ‘made.’

SAMIN-DURR:18:7/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:7/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:7/r3.claim: Ayyuhum may be interrogative: a subject with aḥsanu as predicate, its clause occupying the object position of linabluwهم because testing is a cause of knowing, like asking or looking.
SAMIN-DURR:18:7/r3.anchor: يجوز في " أيهم " وجهان، أحدهما: أن تكون استفهامية مرفوعة

SAMIN-DURR:18:7/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:7/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:7/r4.claim: Alternatively, ayyuhum is a relative pronoun meaning ‘the one who’; aḥsanu predicates an omitted subject, and the clause is its relative clause, with the pronoun substituting for the object of linabluwهم.
SAMIN-DURR:18:7/r4.anchor: أنها موصولة بمعنى الذي " وأحسن " خبر مبتدأ مضمر، والجملة

SAMIN-DURR:18:7/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:7/r5.speaker: سيبويه
SAMIN-DURR:18:7/r5.claim: On the relative analysis, the nominative ending of ayyuhum can be indeclinable: it is formally annexed and the start of its relative clause is omitted, meeting the conditions for building it.
SAMIN-DURR:18:7/r5.anchor: وهذا مذهب سيبويه، وأن تكون للإعراب لأن البناء جائز لا واجب.

SAMIN-DURR:18:7/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:7/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:7/r6.claim: The nominative may instead be inflectional because building is permissible, not obligatory; an anomalous Maryam reading has inflected ayyuhum.
SAMIN-DURR:18:7/r6.anchor: ومن الإعراب ما قرئ به شاذا أيهم أشد على الرحمن

SAMIN-DURR:18:7/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:7/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:7/r7.claim: The cited verse about greeting whichever of the Banu Mālik is best supplies poetic usage for ayyuhum with a nominative ending.

SAMIN-DURR:18:7/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:7/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:7/r8.claim: The pronouns in linabluwهم and ayyuhum refer to the earth’s inhabitants inferred from context; another analysis refers to what is on earth if it means rational beings. Exegetes identify them as shepherds, or scholars, righteous people, and caliphs.
SAMIN-DURR:18:7/r8.anchor: والضمير في " لنبلوهم " و " أيهم " عائد على ما يفهم من السياق

ZAJJAJ:v3p269/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p269/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p269/r1.claim: The adornments on earth are a test; the best in deed is the one who renounces what worldly life has adorned.
ZAJJAJ:v3p269/r1.anchor:
أي اختبارا ومحنة، فالحسن العمل من زهد فيما زين له من
الدنيا،

ZAJJAJ:v3p269/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p269/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p269/r2.claim: أيهم is grammatically a nominative مبتدأ despite its interrogative form, asking which person is better in deed.
ZAJJAJ:v3p269/r2.anchor: و (أيهم) مرفوع بالابتداء، إلا أن لفظه لفظ الاستفهام

ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n5/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n5/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n5/r1.claim: Worldly adornments test people by revealing their moral character through their attitudes toward material goods and benefits.
ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n5/r1.anchor: God lets them reveal their real characters in their respective attitudes - moral or immoral - towards the material goods and benefits

ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n5/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n5/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n5/r2.claim: Refusal of spiritual guidance usually stems from blind worldly attachment and pride in one's achievements.
ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n5/r2.anchor: their excessive, blind attachment to the good of this world, combined with a false pride in what they regard as their own achievements

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Like the previous sūrah, al-Kahf was revealed in the late Makkan conflict, as Quraysh sought to erase the Qur’ānic mission while Jews and Christians backed them indirectly.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Like the previous sūrah, this sūrah was also revealed in that part of the Makkan period when the conflict between good and evil of the Prophet’s preaching mission had entered its final phase.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Quraysh are warned not to let worldly success lead them to reject an obvious truth, since God’s punishment is near if they persist in arrogance.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The Quryash are warned that in the wake of their worldly successes they should not try to arrogantly deny an obvious reality.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Prophet and companions are urged to patience and steadfastness, with hints of migration and glad tidings of coming victories granted by God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The Prophet (sws) and his companions are urged to be patient and steadfast. Certain subtle indications are made of the upcoming phases of migration

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Where the previous sūrah exposed Jews, al-Kahf and Maryam expose Christians; Quraysh risk losing the great opportunity God offers if they follow baseless opponents in rejecting it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Just as in the previous sūrah, S ūrah Banī Isrā’īl, the Jews are exposed, in this sūrah and in the next one – S ūrah Maryam – the Christians are exposed.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Prophet’s task is to warn and give glad tidings; unbelief among rebels reflects neither a defect in the Book nor a shortcoming in his preaching.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The Prophet (sws) is urged to be patient since his only responsibility is to warn and give glad tidings to his nation.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: People’s blindness comes from infatuation with worldly lures; the Prophet should not fret, because the world’s false ornament will be exposed and they will regret their conduct.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The reason for this is that these people have become blind in their infatuation with the lures of this world.

ABUDAWUD:415/r1.author: ABUDAWUD
ABUDAWUD:415/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو الأوزاعي
ABUDAWUD:415/r1.claim: Al-Awzaʿi glosses the earth’s adornment as what is seen on earth yellow in the sunlight.
ABUDAWUD:415/r1.anchor: قَالَ أَبُو عَمْرٍو يَعْنِي الأَوْزَاعِيَّ وَذَلِكَ أَنْ تَرَى، مَا عَلَى الأَرْضِ مِنَ الشَّمْسِ صَفْرَاءَ

BUKHARI:2817/r1.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:2817/r1.speaker: أنس بن مالك عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BUKHARI:2817/r1.claim: Anas reports the Prophet saying that no one in Paradise wishes to return to worldly life, even with all earth's goods, except a martyr who longs to be killed again for the honor he sees; this illustrates the verse's test through earthly adornment.
BUKHARI:2817/r1.anchor: سَمِعْتُ أَنَسَ بْنَ مَالِكٍ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ

IBNHIBBAN:4662/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:4662/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNHIBBAN:4662/r1.claim: Anas reports the Prophet said that only a martyr in Paradise would wish to return despite having all the earth’s goods, so he could be killed ten times for the honor he sees; this shows the greater value of rewarded deeds.
IBNHIBBAN:4662/r1.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "ما من أحد يدخل الجنة يحب أن يرجع إلى الدنيا

MUSLIM:2301/r1.author: MUSLIM
MUSLIM:2301/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUSLIM:2301/r1.claim: The Prophet warns that dying with camels, cattle, or sheep without paying their zakat leaves an obligation unmet; the report illustrates earthly wealth as a test of conduct.
MUSLIM:2301/r1.anchor: والذي نفسي بيده ما على الأرض رجل يموت فيدع إبلا أو بقرا أو غنما لم يؤد زكاتها

MUSLIM:4868/r1.author: MUSLIM
MUSLIM:4868/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUSLIM:4868/r1.claim: The Prophet says Paradise’s people would not trade it for any earthly thing; a martyr alone longs to return and be killed again for the honor witnessed, ranking afterlife reward above worldly goods.
MUSLIM:4868/r1.anchor: عَنْ قَتَادَةَ، قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَنَسَ بْنَ مَالِكٍ، يُحَدِّثُ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ مَا مِنْ أَحَدٍ يَدْخُلُ الْجَنَّةَ يُحِبُّ أَنْ يَرْجِعَ إِلَى الدُّنْيَا

MUSNAD-AHMAD:12003/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:12003/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUSNAD-AHMAD:12003/r1.claim: The Prophet says Paradise's entrant would prefer to stay despite possessing all earthly things; only the martyr wishes to return after seeing the honor granted.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:12003/r1.anchor: عن أنس، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " ما من أحد يدخل الجنة، يحب أن يخرج منها

MUSNAD-AHMAD:12289/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:12289/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUSNAD-AHMAD:12289/r1.claim: The Prophet says a person in Hell would offer everything on earth as ransom, yet had refused the pledge against associating partners with God.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:12289/r1.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " يقال للرجل من أهل النار يوم القيامة: أرأيت لو كان لك ما على الأرض من شيء

MUSNAD-AHMAD:12771/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:12771/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUSNAD-AHMAD:12771/r1.claim: The Prophet says no one in Paradise wants to return despite owning all that is on earth, except a martyr who longs to return and be killed again for the honor.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:12771/r1.anchor: سمعت أنس بن مالك يحدث، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: " ما من أحد يدخل الجنة يحب أن يرجع إلى الدنيا

MUSNAD-AHMAD:13926/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:13926/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUSNAD-AHMAD:13926/r1.claim: The Prophet says no one in Paradise wants to return despite owning all that is on earth, except a martyr who longs to return and be killed again for the honor.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:13926/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قال: سمعت أنس بن مالك، يحدث عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " ما من أحد يدخل الجنة

MUSNAD-AHMAD:22710/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:22710/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUSNAD-AHMAD:22710/r1.claim: The Prophet says the righteous dead do not wish to return to earthly life, except a martyr who longs to be killed again.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:22710/r1.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " ما على الأرض من نفس تموت ولها عند الله خير تحب أن ترجع إليكم إلا المقتول

MUSNAD-AHMAD:22748/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:22748/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUSNAD-AHMAD:22748/r1.claim: The Prophet says the righteous dead do not wish to return to earthly life, except a martyr who longs to be killed again.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:22748/r1.anchor: عبادة بن الصامت حدثهم، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " ما على الأرض من نفس تموت ولها عند الله خير
